title: Deber and tener que: what had to be done

sections.content: You know *tener que* and *deber* from B1 Unit 4: *tener que* says what you have to do, and *deber* says what you should do. The new republics had both kinds of problems. *Tuvieron que* (preterite) says what they had to do at one time; *tenían que* (imperfect) describes a duty that lasted.

items.spanish: Los gobiernos tuvieron que pedir préstamos para pagar a los soldados.
items.english: The governments had to ask for loans to pay the soldiers.

items.spanish: Los artesanos tenían que competir con productos baratos.
items.english: The craftsmen had to compete with cheap products.

items.spanish: Un gobierno debe pensar en cómo va a pagar un préstamo.
items.english: A government should think about how it will pay a loan.

items.spanish: Entonces tuvieron que renegociar las deudas.
items.english: Then they had to renegotiate the debts.

sections.content: *Tener que* + infinitive is a real necessity (*tuvieron que pedir*); *deber* + infinitive is advice or duty (*debe pensar*). Do not add *que* after *deber*.
